summary: Summation No. 22 covers South Korean Interim Government activities for July 1947, prepared by the Statistical Research Division, Office of Administration, under Acting Military Governor Brig. Gen. C. G. Helmick. The month is dominated by the stalled US-USSR Joint Commission over which parties may be consulted, the 19 July assassination of Lyuh Woon-hyung, and the Interim Legislative Assembly's passage of the anti-collaborator law and second reading of a Temporary Constitution. Administration reports detail the new policy for selling vested Japanese residences and small businesses, rent increases, New Korea Company landholdings, Helmick's objections to the franchise law, and the 1948-49 budget directive. Social sections give refugee quotas, public health guidance to provincial advisers, vaccine and narcotics tables, school statistics, Korean National Youth data, and a long press digest. Part III (Economic) is not included. Historians will find full texts of Joint Commission statements, directives and ordinances.
highlights: Lyuh Woon-hyung, leader of the Laboring People's Party, was shot dead in his car in Seoul on 19 July; Han Chi-kun, a young man from North Korea, was arrested, and General Hodge publicly deplored the killing.

The Interim Legislative Assembly passed the Special Law Dealing with National Traitors, Collaborators, and Profiteers (formerly the Anti-Collaborator Bill) on 2 July and by 31 July had passed most articles of a Temporary Constitution on second reading.

On 12 July Helmick announced sale of vested Japanese small businesses and urban residences to Koreans; purchasers pay at least 20 percent down, contracts run up to ten years, and provincial advisory committees will screen buyers.

Helmick's 21 July letter asked the Assembly to reconsider the franchise law, objecting to the voting age of 23, disqualification of ex-prisoners and alleged collaborators, a special northern district, the written-ballot requirement and Supreme Court jurisdiction.

The US-USSR Joint Commission deadlocked from the 37th to the 42nd meeting and beyond over consulting parties linked to the Anti-Trusteeship Committee; Gen. Brown and Soviet chief Shtykov issued rival statements on 15, 21, 27 and 31 July.

A Property Custodian rental decree let rents on vested residences rise up to 300 percent for government employees and up to fifty times 1937 levels for others; the New Korea Company controls 309,658 chungbo of agricultural land.

The National Refugee Board suspended refugee settlement in Seoul from 1 July and set provincial quotas (20 percent each for Kyongsang-pukto, Cholla-pukto and Cholla-namdo); 38,728 people passed through the 38th-parallel camps by June.
Acting Military Governor Helmick said US civilian supply aid to Korea from May 1946 to March 1947 totalled ninety-one million dollars, and rebutted rumors that Korean food was being exported.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover, title page for Summation No. 22 (July 1947), foreword signed by Lt. Col. William Wall O'Hearn, and table of contents.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Short overview of July: property disposal, franchise law, Legislative Assembly action, Lyuh's assassination, Joint Commission, plus a social summary; economic section deferred to the National Economic Board.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Summarizes sale of Japanese property, rental increases, governor transfers, Assembly laws, Lyuh's 19 July assassination, Joint Commission consultation dispute, and Constabulary and Coast Guard activities.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Placeholder page stating the economic section is to be submitted by the National Economic Board.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Provincial health advisers' 14 July conference, UNRRA aid of about one million dollars, penicillin plan, Seoul National University year-end, Olympic celebrations, and bulletin and radio coverage of the Joint Commission.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Detailed government and political reporting (property policy, Assembly, Joint Commission texts) followed by legal developments, police, prisons and internal security; Part III Economic was not submitted.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Full texts of property sale directives, Helmick's franchise-law letter, Assembly debates on collaborators and the constitution, party trends, Joint Commission statements, mail exchange and Foreign Affairs.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Policy and directives for selling Japanese urban residences and small businesses, rent increases, New Korea Company's 309,658 chungbo, governor transfers, franchise letter, budget directive, and US aid statements.

sections.title: Korea Civil Service
sections.summary: Training Division prepared first Performance Rating Reports, due in the first fifteen days of August, and clerical examinations continued in the provinces.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Passage of the Special Law on traitors, collaborators and profiteers; second reading of the Temporary Constitution; vote 39-22 returning governor transfers; Ordinance 118 dispute; July attendance table.

sections.title: Political Activities
sections.summary: Rightist 4 July conference demanded Civil Administrator Ahn's resignation; Leftist joint statements; Lyuh assassinated 19 July; Wedemeyer designated as presidential envoy.

sections.title: US-USSR Joint Commission
sections.summary: Pyongyang sessions 2-3 July, dispute over consulting Anti-Trusteeship Committee parties, statements by Brown and Shtykov, Koreans in Japan's message, and party-membership tables of 118 South Korean groups.

sections.title: Interzone Activities
sections.summary: Two exchanges of mail with the Soviet zone, on 12 July (10,643 letters sent north) and 26 July (10,108 letters sent north).

sections.title: Foreign Affairs
sections.summary: 18,672 Koreans apprehended entering Japan illegally, 300 permits for Chinese repatriation, Dr. Moon Chang-wook's US mission for fifty students, and July repatriation ship tables.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Court dockets, juvenile courts and new ordinances, then public safety: Lyuh's assassination, provincial disturbances, National Police strength of 28,552, prison population of 19,833, and Constabulary and Coast Guard news.

sections.title: Legal
sections.summary: Criminal dockets brought current by 20 July; 1,240 juvenile cases in five months; texts of Ordinances 142 (income tax), 143 (Crop Reporting Board), 145 (Foreign Exchange Bank), and Executive Order 4 making Korean official.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Law and order, police, prison and internal security reports for July with statistical tables.

sections.title: Law and Order
sections.summary: Lyuh Woon-hyung assassinated 19 July, General Hodge's statement, and mob clashes in Cholla-pukto, Kyongsang-namdo, Kyongsang-pukto and Chungchong-pukto.

sections.title: Police
sections.summary: Crime Laboratory completed 45 cases in June (2,103 examinations to date); 3,500 Basic English manuals printed; police strength 28,552 and 1,977 installations.

sections.title: Prisons
sections.summary: Kwangju Prison industries, 10,000 blankets received, and June tables: 19,833 prisoners against capacity of 21,600, 25 deaths, 340 in reformatories.

sections.title: Internal Security
sections.summary: Constabulary and prisoners helped Kunsan farmers transplant rice; Coast Guard rescued rice ship off Ullung-do on 26 July; supply receipts of 17,563 cots and 1,214 tents.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health and welfare, education and culture, and public information for July, including health guidance letter, refugee quotas, vaccine and school tables, and a long press digest.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Adviser conference and guidance letter, refugee quotas, welfare institutions, UNRRA and LARA aid, nursing, dental, pharmacy, veterinary and laboratory reports, sanitation and communicable disease figures.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Provincial health advisers met 14 July; letter covers disease control, vital statistics, veterinary and nursing advice, medical supply distribution and welfare; organizational chart as reorganized May 1947.

sections.title: Public Welfare
sections.summary: Refugee influx fell thirty percent in June; Seoul settlement suspended 1 July; provincial quotas set; cumulative repatriation totals; 38,728 people cared for in camps.

sections.title: Welfare Institutions and Agencies
sections.summary: 317 homeless children and adults placed in institutions on 24-25 July; UNRRA program closed 30 June after about one million dollars; first LARA supplies arrived.

sections.title: Women's Bureau
sections.summary: Monday lectures on Korean industry, home economics classes for telephone exchange women, and a Women's Section opened in Seoul's Bureau of Public Welfare on 1 July.

sections.title: Medical Services
sections.summary: Plan formulated for distributing and accounting for three metric tons of UNRRA penicillin.

sections.title: Nursing Affairs
sections.summary: Inspection of hospitals in Pusan, Chinju, Taegu and Masan found lack of funds; nursing curriculum revised so third-year students can specialize.

sections.title: Dental Affairs
sections.summary: Only 80 of 242 applicants admitted to the Dental College; three rural dental teams left 16 July; 491 licensed dentists in South Korea.

sections.title: Pharmaceutical Affairs
sections.summary: Thirty of seventy new-medicine applications approved, 567 pharmacists registered, narcotics classes held, and monthly tables of confiscated narcotics from July 1946 to July 1947.

sections.title: Veterinary Affairs
sections.summary: First veterinary medicine school established within Seoul National University; 175 bicycles sought for veterinarians short of transport.

sections.title: Laboratories
sections.summary: Cholera vaccine production figures (5,375,300 cc on hand 25 July), veterinary biologicals consolidated at Pusan, and tables of vaccine stocks at Seoul, Anyang and Pusan institutes.

sections.title: Housing
sections.summary: Winter 1946-47 study put South Korea's population at 19,300,000, up twenty-two percent since 1944; Seoul grew 38.2 percent.

sections.title: Vital Statistics
sections.summary: Directive ended duplicate vital statistics transcripts previously prepared for the Census Division of the Office of Administration.

sections.title: Sanitation
sections.summary: Inspectors sought the yellow dye "killing sugar" in restaurants and bakeries; rodent control continued; June tables of food and beverage establishments by province.

sections.title: Preventive Medicine
sections.summary: 2,864 communicable disease cases in June (1,073 typhoid), down about forty-five percent from June 1946; typhoid inoculation program to start about 15 September.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University disturbances, summer institutes, textbook distribution, school statistics, Korea's admission to the 1948 Olympics, and Korean National Youth activity.

sections.title: Education
sections.summary: Eight students expelled and 169 suspended at Seoul National University; 560 diplomas awarded; 282 attended Summer Institute; 427,760 textbooks distributed; school statistics at 31 May.

sections.title: Culture
sections.summary: Olympic celebration at Seoul Stadium on 19 July before 50,000 spectators; National Youth held 13,080 discussion meetings, graduated 197 leaders, membership of 147,481.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: Information programs, newsreels, Korean Broadcasting System programming of 341 hours, publications, newspaper circulation table and a digest of press opinion on politics, the Joint Commission and Lyuh's assassination.

sections.title: Information Programs
sections.summary: News posters moved indoors because of heavy rain; 1,067 discussion groups with 34,311 members organized by 7 July.

sections.title: Motion Pictures
sections.summary: Monthly newsreel to start in August; Newsreel No. 21 issued 26 July; 30 films reviewed in July (18 Korean, 11 American, 1 Japanese).

sections.title: Radio
sections.summary: Text of Kim Yong-jeung's 8 July broadcast, first Man on the Street program on 27 July, 341 hours of KBS broadcasting, and a typical daily schedule.

sections.title: Publications
sections.summary: Dr. C. C. Hahn's Principles of Democracy published; Farmers' Weekly suspended because of paper shortage; Marshall's 1 July press speech translated and distributed.

sections.title: Press and Public Opinion
sections.summary: Circulation table of 21 Seoul dailies, then press comment on the franchise law, Joint Commission, Wedemeyer visit, Lyuh's death, Rhee-Hodge dispute, and a poll in which 67 percent favored the interim government.
